name: Zacchaeus
charge: Extortion as chief of the publicans
summary: A rich chief tax-collector of Jericho climbed a sycamore to see Jesus and was called down by name. Standing in his house he said: the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold.
offense: The publican's trade as commonly practiced: assessment by false accusation and extortion, which Leviticus 6 classes with theft and fraud. Fourfold was the law's rate for a stolen sheep, the highest ordinary restitution, and Zacchaeus chose it for himself.
judgment: This day is salvation come to this house, forsomuch as he also is a son of Abraham. The restitution was not the price of the salvation but its evidence: fruits meet for repentance, the very thing John had told the publicans to bring.

entries.commentary: If a man steal an ox or a sheep and kill it or sell it, he restores five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep. We are in a different situation where we do not keep oxen and sheep, but the principle of restitution still applies among brothers and sisters in the body: if something is stolen, the law written here governs the payback. Do not be stealing.

If a thief be found breaking up means breaking in. He entered your home and you defended yourself and he died: that is what is called self-defense today, and no blood is shed for him, meaning there is no judgment. The judgment was already passed in the breaking in. If the sun be risen upon him, the thief got away, and there shall be blood shed for him means there shall be a judgment; then the verse gives the judgment. He makes full restitution, and if he have nothing he is sold for his theft: not sold into slavery, but into work servitude until he pays off the debt of what he stole. If the theft be found in his hand alive, he restores double. Verse three covers the thief who already got rid of what he stole; verse four covers the one still holding it.

These are self-explanatory: if a man lets his beast feed in another man's field or vineyard, he makes restitution of the best of his own field and vineyard; and he that kindles a fire that consumes another man's corn surely makes restitution.

If a man deliver money or stuff to his neighbor to keep and it be stolen, the thief found pays double. If the thief be not found, the master of the house is brought unto the judges, to see whether he put his hand unto his neighbor's goods, whether he was part of a scheme to deceive the owner out of his goods. For all manner of trespass, whether for ox, ass, sheep, raiment, or any lost thing, both parties come before the judges, and whom the judges condemn pays double unto his neighbor.

If a beast delivered to a neighbor to keep die or be hurt or driven away, no man seeing it, an oath of the Lord is between them both. In layman's terms he swears: I did not take the stuff, I did not set you up, I do not know where it is. The owner accepts the oath and the matter ends there; it is not to be spoken of again. Paul uses this civil law to show how the Most High is unchangeable. An oath for confirmation is the end of all strife; God confirmed his counsel by an oath, and by two immutable things, that it is impossible for God to lie and that he will not take back what went out of his mouth, we have strong consolation. The same way, once the oath of this law is applied, the matter is over.

If the thing kept be stolen from him, he makes restitution; if it be torn in pieces, he brings it for witness and does not make it good. If a man borrow ought of his neighbor, ought meaning anything, and it be hurt or die with the owner not present, he surely makes it good. You borrowed it, it got messed up, you owe the man. But if the owner be with it, or if it be an hired thing, it came for its hire. If you came to plow a man's field for ten shekels with your own donkey and your donkey breaks his leg, you cannot expect the owner to pay for your own faulty equipment; the same as a business loan today, the property owner is not liable when your own equipment breaks down.

If a man entice a maid that is not betrothed and lie with her, he shall surely endow her to be his wife; he has to sign the papers. He is at fault for not going through the proper channels of marriage, and she is at fault for being enticed and laying down. The proper channel was that the father married off the daughter. To marry thy daughter is to perform a weighty matter, for the father gives her over to that man for the rest of her life and is out of all watching over her; so she is to be given to a man of understanding, one keeping the commandments as a wise man. In our own land the daughter went from her father's house to a husband's house with the blessing of the father.

Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live: witchcraft goes into horoscopes, palm readings, and all things of that nature. Whosoever lieth with a beast, bestiality, shall surely be put to death. He that sacrificeth unto any god save unto the Lord only shall be utterly destroyed.

This is twofold, and first and foremost the stranger is your brother from a different area, our own people. [Leviticus 25](/bible/leviticus/25) shows it: if thy brother be waxen poor, though he be a stranger or a sojourner, sojourn meaning travel, thou shalt relieve him that he may live with thee. A brother of another tribe who falls on hard times and travels down to live with you is that stranger; neither vex him nor oppress him, for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt.

Ye shall not afflict any widow or fatherless child. A wife without a husband already has a hard life, and a son or daughter without a father the same; do not make their life harder than it already is. If thou afflict them in any wise and they cry unto the Most High, he will surely hear their cry, and his wrath shall wax hot: he will kill you with the sword, and your own wives shall be widows and your children fatherless. That is the Lord's plain warning against mistreating those less fortunate.

Usury means interest. You cannot charge your brother or sister interest: if you lend twenty dollars, you get twenty dollars back, nothing more, nothing less; no little bit more off the top. This is the same law read in [Leviticus 25:36-37](/bible/leviticus/25#v36).

If thou take thy neighbor's raiment to pledge, deliver it unto him by that the sun goeth down, for that is his covering only; wherein shall he sleep? The tunics and overcoats worn then were also sleeping garments to keep a man warm at night, especially the poor. A well-off man does not have to work for you; this speaks of the less fortunate who extend their services for money and give what is most valuable to them, their raiment, as the pledge. If he cries unto the Most High, he will hear, for he is gracious.

Thou shalt not revile the gods means do not hate or speak evil of your leaders. The word gods here is the leaders over you: the Most High says in the psalm, I have said, Ye are gods, and all of you are children of the Most High, speaking of us. [Acts 23](/bible/acts/23) is the example: when Paul spoke against the high priest, they that stood by said, Revilest thou God's high priest? And Paul answered, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people, quoting this very verse.

Thou shalt not delay to offer the first of thy ripe fruits and of thy liquors, and the firstborn of thy sons shalt thou give unto me. The firstborn sons that opened the matrix were consecrated unto the Lord, and the father redeemed them back from the priest with shekels. Likewise with the oxen and the sheep: seven days the firstling stayed with his dam, his mother, and on the eighth day it was given. The Lord did not want it too young, taken as soon as it popped out; it had to be its appointed time with the mother, then brought to the priest.

Ye shall be holy men unto me: neither shall ye eat any flesh that is torn of beasts in the field; ye shall cast it to the dogs. This is twofold, and the dogs are the strangers of other nations, the aliens and foreigners. Always get the context of the law, because sometimes the stranger is your brother and sometimes it is literally the other nations. [Deuteronomy 14:21](/bible/deuteronomy/14#v21) doubles this law: that which dieth of itself thou shalt give unto the stranger that is in thy gates, or sell it unto an alien, for thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God. Cast the torn flesh to the other nations; ye shall not eat it, because ye are holy people.

If a soul lie unto his neighbour in that which was delivered him to keep, or in fellowship, or deceive his neighbour, or find that which was lost and lie concerning it, and swear falsely, the Lord counts all of it as a thing taken away by violence: verse 4 says he shall restore that which he took violently away. Deceiving your neighbour, going into agreement and not holding up your end, or lying about what was given you to hold is a violent act toward your neighbour, and a Ponzi scheme or pyramid scheme sits right in that law. He shall restore it in the principal: the value of what was taken had to be given back, with more added on top. A sorry would not settle it with the Lord; you could end up in debt for years over sticky fingers. Stealing was not a sin unto death, but the Lord made the restitution heavy so you would never commit it again. It goes back to the commandment, thou shalt not steal, and to the civil law where an ox was restored fivefold and a sheep fourfold.

The trespass offering was a ram without blemish, perfect as the Most High made it, and the priest made an atonement for him before the Lord and it was forgiven him. The sacrifice stood in your place for your sin. The whole law of sacrifice points to Christ, who came in the volume of the book. He is the offering without blemish and the atonement, and who has become the high priest is Jesus the Christ. Israel became the enemy of the Most High by sin. There are two kinds of enemies: the nations that are the natural enemies of the Most High, and Israel, who rebelled and vexed his holy spirit, and he was turned to be their enemy. Through the death of his Son the nation is reconciled, brought back together with its God. The letters of Paul were written to Israelites living in those lands and called by their names, Romans and Corinthians, the same way we are called American or Jamaican today; written today they would be the letter to the Jamaicans or the letter to the Puerto Ricans.

The burnt offering burned upon the altar all night unto the morning, and the fire of the altar was burning in it. When Exodus says kindle no fire on the sabbath day, that speaks of making food; the Levites were commanded to keep a fire burning on the altar continually, sabbath included. Christ used this very law on the Pharisees: have ye not read how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless? The priests had fire going in the temple every sabbath by commandment. I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: the Most High desired the knowledge of God and obedience more than burnt offerings. Israel leaned so heavily on the sacrifices instead of applying the commandments that they were confounded and could not see Christ as the Son of God when he came. Jeremiah carries the same word: I spake not unto your fathers concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices, but this thing commanded I them, obey my voice. Yet they hearkened not, but walked in the counsels of their evil heart and went backward and not forward; speak all these words unto them, but they will not hearken. That is seen every sabbath on the streets.

The priest put on his linen garment and his linen breeches upon his flesh. The priests were men, not women, and breeches are pants; they were made for the men. The ashes of the burnt offering were carried forth without the camp unto a clean place. Christ fulfilled that figure: they led him away out of the city to crucify him at Golgotha, the place of a skull; he suffered without the gate. Hebrews draws the lesson: let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach. Put away the sacrifice as it was carried outside the temple, and come out unto Christ.

The fire upon the altar shall be burning in it; it shall not be put out. The priest burnt wood on it every morning, and that included the sabbath; the fire shall ever be burning upon the altar, and it shall never go out. This is exactly what Christ went into in Matthew 12: the priests profane the sabbath and are blameless, because the commanded altar fire never went out.

This is the law of the meat offering. The meat offering is not flesh; it is grain, fine flour with oil and frankincense. A handful was burnt upon the altar for a sweet savour, and the remainder Aaron and his sons ate unleavened in the holy place. It shall be a statute for ever in your generations: the law is spiritual. To understand how a perpetual statute of sacrifice pointed to Christ, the Spirit of Christ had to dwell in you; Paul himself did not understand until Christ touched him on the way to Damascus. Christ told the disciples the Comforter would teach them all things and bring all things to their remembrance. Unless the Spirit of the Lord deals with you, you will never understand the Bible or the laws; that is why there was such contention between Christ and the Pharisees, for the Spirit had not revealed to them who he was.

This is the offering of Aaron and of his sons in the day when he is anointed: the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour for a meat offering perpetual, half in the morning and half at night, baked with oil in a pan. The meat offering is again actual flour, grain. Every meat offering for the priest was wholly burnt; it was not eaten. The priest's own offering went completely to the Lord.

This is the law of the sin offering: in the place where the burnt offering is killed shall the sin offering be killed before the LORD; it is most holy. Christ was the sin offering, and he was most holy. Christ did no sin, neither was guile, which is deceit, found in his mouth; when he was reviled, he reviled not again. He kept his Father's commandments and abode in his love, leaving us an example that we should follow his steps; if you do not keep the commandments of God you are not following his steps. The blood was not eaten: the sin offering whose blood was brought into the tabernacle to reconcile was not eaten but burnt in the fire. Israel does not mess with the blood; Esau eats the blood, not us.

Every leper, every one that hath an issue, and whosoever is defiled by the dead, male and female, was put out without the camp, that they defile not their camps in the midst whereof the Most High dwelt. And the children of Israel did so. Israel is referred to as a camp all through these chapters. The Lord is gathering his camp back together again to come and deliver us; if you are not in a camp, get in a camp. Inside the camp we consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works; the stronger in faith exhort the weaker to keep striving and endure to the end. If you are not gathered you cannot do that, and you do a disservice to the Lord and to your people. Separating yourself after receiving the knowledge of the truth is willful sin, and there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, but a fearful looking for of judgment; that is doing despite unto the spirit of grace that woke us up in these last days.

When a man or woman commits a trespass against the Lord, they shall confess their sin and recompense the trespass with the principal thereof plus the fifth part, given unto him against whom the trespass was done. [Exodus 22](/bible/exodus/22) is the chapter of those civil matters and repayments; the Lord laid the payment on you so you would learn not to do it again. If the man have no kinsman, the trespass was recompensed unto the Lord, even to the priest, beside the ram of the atonement. The atonement now is Christ; we no longer take a ram to a priest, because Christ became the atonement and we ask forgiveness through him. Christ is the advocate and the propitiation, the mercy, for our sins; there is no more Levite priest sacrifice, for he is the mediator between us and the Most High now. The whole world in that verse is the whole world of the nation of Israel.

Every offering of the holy things brought unto the priest was his, because the Levites had no inheritance of land as the other tribes did. Levi was scattered in every land, in Ephraim, in Dan, in Zebulun, in Judah, in Benjamin, so the people could bring the sacrifice to them; Levi had no plot to cultivate crops on, and was fed by the people of the Lord.

If a man's wife go aside and lie with another carnally, hid from the eyes of her husband with no witness, and the spirit of jealousy come upon him, there is a law for it. The spirit of jealousy is the Lord putting it on the husband that something is not right: the routine changes, and he begins questioning and seeing things differently, whether she be defiled or not defiled. The man brought his wife unto the priest with the tenth part of an ephah of barley meal, no oil and no frankincense upon it, for it is an offering of jealousy, an offering of memorial, bringing iniquity to remembrance; the Lord said do not make this offering sweet.

The priest set the woman before the Lord, took holy water in an earthen vessel with the dust of the floor of the tabernacle, and uncovered the woman's head. Verse 18 is a precept that our sisters had their heads covered. A wig is not the covering; the covered head is a custom, a tradition, and our heritage.

The priest charged her by an oath: if no man have lain with thee, be thou free from this bitter water that causeth the curse; but if thou hast gone aside to another instead of thy husband, the Lord make thy thigh to rot and thy belly to swell. The Most High is hard on his daughters for a reason, and he was not playing with that judgment. The woman had to answer Amen, amen. If you would not agree to drink the water, you showed yourself guilty already, and the guilty were stoned. Surely your sin shall find you out; there is nothing you can hide.

The priest wrote the curses in a book and blotted them out with the bitter water, waved the jealousy offering before the Lord, burnt the memorial upon the altar, and caused the woman to drink. If she was defiled, the water became bitter, her belly swelled and her thigh rotted, and the woman became a curse among her people, a plague she could not get rid of. If she was not defiled, she was free and shall conceive seed; the husband was simply tripping, and she was clear.

This is the law of jealousies, when a wife goeth aside or when the spirit of jealousy cometh upon a husband: the priest executed upon her all this law, the man was guiltless from iniquity, and the woman, if guilty, bore her iniquity.

The Most High sent Nathan unto David, who told him of two men in one city, one rich and one poor. The rich man had many flocks and herds, but the poor man had nothing save one little ewe lamb he had bought and nourished up, which was unto him as a daughter. When a traveler came, the rich man spared his own flock and took the poor man's lamb. David's anger was greatly kindled, and he said the man that had done this shall surely die and restore the lamb fourfold, because he had no pity. Nathan came to David with a parable. When David judged that the man deserved to die for taking the poor man's one lamb, he was unknowingly pronouncing sentence on himself.

Nathan said unto David, Thou art the man. Thus saith the Most High: I anointed thee king over Israel, delivered thee out of the hand of Saul, gave thee thy master's house and wives, and the house of Israel and of Judah, and would have given thee more. Wherefore hast thou despised the commandment to do evil, killing Uriah the Hittite with the sword and taking his wife, slaying him with the sword of the children of Ammon? The Most High said if David would have just asked, He would have given him anything, for He had already given him the kingdom, Saul's house, and protection from Saul. The commandment David despised was what was read in [Deuteronomy 27](/bible/deuteronomy/27). There is a term called suicide by cop; David committed murder by the hand of another nation, because he set the whole thing up.

Thus saith the Most High: Now therefore the sword shall never depart from thine house, because thou hast despised me and taken the wife of Uriah to be thy wife. Behold, I will raise up evil against thee out of thine own house, and I will take thy wives before thine eyes and give them unto thy neighbour, who shall lie with them in the sight of the sun. Thou didst it secretly, but I will do this thing before all Israel and before the sun. As the four chapters go on, and beyond, you are going to see the fruition of what just happened worked out in David's own house.

David said unto Nathan, I have sinned against the Most High. Nathan said the Most High hath also put away thy sin; thou shalt not die. Howbeit, because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of the Most High to blaspheme, the child also that is born unto thee shall surely die. The judgment of David was that child being put to death. This goes back to Exodus 34: the Most High keeps mercy and forgives iniquity, but will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquities of the fathers upon the children. David got pardoned, but he did not get cleared; the punishment was still coming, one part the men of Israel dying in battle, the other his son having to die and his house having nothing but trouble.

Nathan departed, and the Most High struck the child, so that it was very sick. David besought God for the child, fasted, and lay all night upon the earth, refusing to rise or eat with the elders of his house. On the seventh day the child died, and the servants feared to tell him. When David perceived by their whispering that the child was dead, he arose, washed, anointed himself, changed his apparel, worshiped in the house of the Most High, and then ate bread. When asked why, he said that while the child lived he fasted and wept, for who could tell whether God would be gracious; but now the child was dead, he could not bring him back, he would go to him but the child would not return to him. David did all the fasting and prayer before the child died because he knew it was of the Most High that this would happen; no amount of prayer would bring the child back. David was content, saying he did not want it to happen but had no choice in the matter, for the Most High had said it would be so.

David comforted Bathsheba his wife, went in unto her, and she bare a son, and he called his name Solomon; and the Most High loved him, and sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet, who called his name Jedidiah, because of the Most High. Through David's judgment, Solomon was still able to be born; it was all part of the plan of the Most High. The backup master plan behind everything was Christ, who still had to be born through David's lineage; David was still loved and still forgiven, which shows repentance, and that even the mighty among us can fall and yet rise back up.

Joab fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon and took the royal city, then sent for David to gather the rest of the people and take the city, lest it be called after Joab's name. David gathered all the people, went to Rabbah, took it, and took the king's crown of a talent of gold with the precious stones, and set it on his head. He brought forth great spoil, put the people to labor under saws and axes of iron and to the brickkiln, and did so unto all the cities of Ammon, then returned to Jerusalem. David won against the children of Ammon once again. What we gather from these four chapters is that David was called, he was king, a very mighty man, but he slipped and fell; he had godly sorrow, and in that godly sorrow he was not put to death. If he had been, there would be no Solomon, and through that no Christ. The only one perfect in this world was Christ, in whom there was no iniquity; but the men before us, when they failed, had godly sorrow, repented, and kept the commandments of the Most High even after they fell, rising back up again. --- Topics: [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)
The rulers of that hour are named, and Annas and Caiaphas are both called high priests. There was to be one, and the naming of two shows how far out of order that priesthood had come.
John preaches the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins, as it is written in the book of the words of Esaias: the voice of one crying in the wilderness.

O generation of vipers, bring forth therefore fruits worthy of repentance, and begin not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father. Being dipped in water without works that go with it is not what is written here. The fruits worthy of repentance are the works.

He that hath two coats, let him impart to him that hath none. The publicans are told to exact no more than that which is appointed them, and the soldiers to do violence to no man, neither accuse any falsely, and be content with their wages.

I indeed baptize you with water; but one mightier than I cometh, he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost and with fire, and he will gather the wheat into his garner, but the chaff he will burn with fire unquenchable.
Herod, being reproved by him for Herodias his brother Philip's wife, and for all the evils which he had done, added yet this above all, that he shut up John in prison.

Jesus being baptized and praying, the heaven was opened, and the Holy Ghost descended in a bodily shape like a dove upon him, and a voice came from heaven, Thou art my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased.

Jesus began to be about thirty years of age, being, as was supposed, the son of Joseph, which was the son of Heli. Heli was the father of Mary, so this line is reckoned through the son-in-law. The generations run back through Nathan and David, through Judah, Jacob, Isaac and Abraham, through Sem and Noe, and to Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.

verses.text: And Jesus entered and passed through Jericho.
And, behold, there was a man named Zaccheus, which was the chief among the publicans, and he was rich.
And he sought to see Jesus who he was; and could not for the press, because he was little of stature.
And he ran before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him: for he was to pass that way.
And when Jesus came to the place, he looked up, and saw him, and said unto him, Zaccheus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house.
And he made haste, and came down, and received him joyfully.
And when they saw it, they all murmured, saying, That he was gone to be guest with a man that is a sinner.
And Zaccheus stood, and said unto the Lord; Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold.
And Jesus said unto him, This day is salvation come to this house, forsomuch as he also is a son of Abraham.
For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.
If a man shall steal an ox, or a sheep, and kill it, or sell it; he shall restore five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.
And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,

If a soul sin, and commit a trespass against the Lord, and lie unto his neighbour in that which was delivered him to keep, or in fellowship, or in a thing taken away by violence, or hath deceived his neighbour;
Or have found that which was lost, and lieth concerning it, and sweareth falsely; in any of all these that a man doeth, sinning therein:

Then it shall be, because he hath sinned, and is guilty, that he shall restore that which he took violently away, or the thing which he hath deceitfully gotten, or that which was delivered him to keep, or the lost thing which he found,

Or all that about which he hath sworn falsely; he shall even restore it in the principal, and shall add the fifth part more thereto, and give it unto him to whom it appertaineth, in the day of his trespass offering.
Speak unto the children of Israel, When a man or woman shall commit any sin that men commit, to do a trespass against the Lord, and that person be guilty;

Then they shall confess their sin which they have done: and he shall recompense his trespass with the principal thereof, and add unto it the fifth part thereof, and give it unto him against whom he hath trespassed.
And he shall restore the lamb fourfold, because he did this thing, and because he had no pity.
Then came also publicans to be baptized, and said unto him, Master, what shall we do?
And he said unto them, Exact no more than that which is appointed you.

Bring forth therefore fruits worthy of repentance, and begin not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, That God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.

lawsResolved.text: Stolen livestock which is slaughtered is to be repaid four or five times.
If one gains property or money by way of a false report, lying, deceit, or extortion, he shall make full restitution plus an additional fifth part of its value.

In civil trespasses involving property deceitfully obtained, the person guilty shall confess his crime and make restitution in full for his wrong, and add to it one-fifth of it, and give it to him whom he has wronged.
A personal trespass that results in a loss of property is to be repaid in the principal amount plus an additional fifth part added to it.
True repentance is evidenced by one's fruits.

And, behold, there was a man named Zaccheus, which was the chief among the publicans, and he was rich.
And he sought to see Jesus who he was; and could not for the press, because he was little of stature.
And he ran before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him: for he was to pass that way.
And when Jesus came to the place, he looked up, and saw him, and said unto him, Zaccheus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house.
And he made haste, and came down, and received him joyfully.
And when they saw it, they all murmured, saying, That he was gone to be guest with a man that is a sinner.
And Zaccheus stood, and said unto the Lord; Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold.
And Jesus said unto him, This day is salvation come to this house, forsomuch as he also is a son of Abraham.
For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.
If a man shall steal an ox, or a sheep, and kill it, or sell it; he shall restore five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.
And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,

If a soul sin, and commit a trespass against the Lord, and lie unto his neighbour in that which was delivered him to keep, or in fellowship, or in a thing taken away by violence, or hath deceived his neighbour;
Or have found that which was lost, and lieth concerning it, and sweareth falsely; in any of all these that a man doeth, sinning therein:

Then it shall be, because he hath sinned, and is guilty, that he shall restore that which he took violently away, or the thing which he hath deceitfully gotten, or that which was delivered him to keep, or the lost thing which he found,

Or all that about which he hath sworn falsely; he shall even restore it in the principal, and shall add the fifth part more thereto, and give it unto him to whom it appertaineth, in the day of his trespass offering.
Speak unto the children of Israel, When a man or woman shall commit any sin that men commit, to do a trespass against the Lord, and that person be guilty;

Then they shall confess their sin which they have done: and he shall recompense his trespass with the principal thereof, and add unto it the fifth part thereof, and give it unto him against whom he hath trespassed.
And he shall restore the lamb fourfold, because he did this thing, and because he had no pity.
Then came also publicans to be baptized, and said unto him, Master, what shall we do?
And he said unto them, Exact no more than that which is appointed you.

Bring forth therefore fruits worthy of repentance, and begin not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, That God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.
